state.decision: How a local CSV file becomes a data source of a graphic project (task 121 slices 2 and 3, row 11.153, Figma B4 'Players.csv, file, 48 rows'). Asked BEFORE the service reader and the persistence are built (claude-grapix-f1, 25 Nov 2026).
state.facts: Slice 1 is built: a strict reader from CSV bytes to a text table or a named fault with its line (delimiter stated by the caller; UTF-8 only; blank lines only at the end; ragged rows, empty or repeated column names, stray or unterminated quotes refused; stated limits 16 MiB, 100,000 rows, 256 columns, 64 KiB a cell; cells exact). A GrapiX project is a named .gpx folder like an XPression .xpf, holding scenes, Footage and Assets (Assets/Images, Videos, Audio, Models, Fonts); importing an asset COPIES the file into the project as a stream beside the destination and renames it into place after a hash check, and a different file at the same name is refused by name, so a project is portable and a scene never depends on a path outside it. Plan row 19.1 (ADR-0005, not yet written) will fix revision pinning of data and a failure policy per field (refuse, hold last good, or warn); 19.2 defines the typed DataSource, DataTable, DataRecord and DataField contract with a source revision, timestamp and staleness state, and says a schema change is a named event, never silent; 19.4 later reads CSV, Excel, JSON and XML from a file with a file watch, and detects and names schema drift. Row 11.54: each template field declares its own type, range and length, so the types of a source's columns come from the graphic's fields, not from the CSV. A producer typically exports a players list from a spreadsheet, then edits and re-exports it several times before and during an event; the same file name is re-exported over the old one. A graphic published to Playout carries revision-pinned data (a take must be reproducible).
state.built: Only the strict reader (Shared/contracts/src/csv_table.rs). No source, no storage, no service reader yet.

storage.instructions: Where does the data of a CSV file source live once it is added to a project?

criteria.A: A copy in the project (for example Data/Players.csv, filed like an asset: streamed, hash-checked, a different file at the same name refused by name), read from the copy; the original path is kept only as a label and a place to offer 'Update from file'. A project stays portable and a take stays reproducible.
criteria.B: A reference: the project stores the original path and reads the file from there every time.
criteria.C: Both at once: read the original live and keep a snapshot copy only as a fallback.

update.instructions: What should happen when the producer re-exports the file and the original on disk differs from the project's copy?

criteria.A: Nothing automatic. The source says 'Changed on disk'; an explicit 'Update from file' reads the new file, shows what changed (rows, and columns added or removed by name) and the copy is replaced only when the user accepts. A column that disappeared and has bound fields is named as such. The old copy is kept as the previous revision until accepted.
criteria.B: Replace the copy silently each time the original changes.
criteria.C: Replace the copy automatically but show a notice afterwards.

drift.instructions: How should a changed set of column names be reported when a file is updated?

criteria.A: As a named schema change: columns added, columns removed, and a different order, each by exact name. A rename is never guessed (it is one removed and one added). It is a named event and never applied silently.
criteria.B: Match columns by position and treat a different name at the same position as a rename.
criteria.C: Match by fuzzy name similarity and carry bindings over.

identity.instructions: How is a record (a row) identified for the Test records table and for the Publish screen's Test row?

criteria.A: By its row number in the file (1-based, counting data rows, the header excluded), always shown with the row's own text; a later slice may let the user name a key column, and a key column with an empty or repeated value is then refused by name.
criteria.B: By its first column, assumed unique.
criteria.C: By a generated random id stored beside the row.

access.instructions: Which files may the service read as a CSV source?

criteria.A: Only the path the operator picked in the Editor's own file picker (the shell hands the path to the service); the service reads a regular file only, checks its size against the limit BEFORE reading it, refuses a directory, a device or a missing file by name, and the MCP and control plane never pass a path (an AI client cannot point the service at a file).
criteria.B: Any path from any caller, including MCP tools.
criteria.C: Only files already inside the project folder.
